evals.prompt: I have network data and want to check loading over time. Find overloaded lines and show results.
evals.title: Power-Flow find high loading lines
evals.expected_output: A working Python script that loads PGM JSON data, runs batch power flow using PowerGridModel or PowerGridModelInterface, identifies overloaded lines (loading > 80%), and produces a matplotlib plot showing loading over time for the worst offenders. The script should run successfully and produce a plot file.

evals.title: Power-Flow Input Validation Report
evals.prompt: Validate network data. Check for any issues. Generate a report with findings.
evals.expected_output: A markdown file at data/synthetic_pgm_data_20260531T143646Z/validation_report.md listing hard validation failures, likely modeling mistakes, and realism anomalies for the synthetic power-flow fixture. Code or commands used to run the validation should be shown.
expectations: A markdown report file is created at the requested synthetic-data path or another clearly named output location
The report references using power-grid-model's validate_input_data or assert_valid_input_data function
The report identifies the fixture as a synthetic medium-voltage power-flow dataset with about 101 nodes, 100 symmetric loads, and one source
The report includes at least one engineering or realism finding beyond a simple 'all clear', such as mixed-sign load injections or unusually large individual load magnitudes

evals.title: Batch Power-Flow Results Interpretation
evals.prompt: I have batch power flow results. Tell me what happened - voltages, branch loading, losses, and what it means for operations.
evals.expected_output: A written explanation covering the synthetic batch power-flow results: voltage profile, branch loading, losses, source/load reactive behavior, and a plain-language operations conclusion.
expectations: A written interpretation report is saved to a file in the outputs directory
The report identifies that the file is a 192-step batch sym_output result rather than a single snapshot
The report discusses that node voltages are broadly close to nominal in the sampled synthetic feeder instead of claiming collapse-level undervoltage
The report addresses branch loading and source reactive support using the actual line/source outputs from the synthetic dataset
The report contains a plain-language or operator-facing conclusion section

evals.title: State-Estimation Sensor Coverage and Quality Diagnosis
evals.prompt: Look at the state estimation data. How good is the sensor coverage? What should I check for bad results?
evals.expected_output: A diagnosis report that summarizes the sensorized synthetic dataset, evaluates state-estimation readiness from available measurements, and gives a numbered checklist for validating estimation quality without relying on hidden ground truth.
expectations: A diagnosis report file is saved to the outputs directory
The report separates findings into at least two categories such as sensor/input coverage and estimator result quality
The report identifies that the synthetic input includes about 101 voltage sensors and 101 power sensors
The report identifies that measurement noise is intentional and should be assessed against sigma fields, residual trends, or temporal consistency rather than treated as raw data corruption
The report provides at least one concrete next check such as reviewing the largest residuals, inspecting voltage trajectories, or checking source injections over the 192-step batch

evals.title: Run and Reproduce Batch Power Flow, Cross-Check Against Reference
evals.prompt: Run power flow on the network and compare with reference results. Show convergence status, key metrics, and any differences.
evals.expected_output: A Python script that loads the data with PGM-IO, runs batch power flow via PowerGridModel.calculate_power_flow(), and outputs a convergence table, per-scenario KPI table, and a numeric cross-check against the reference output file.
expectations: The solution imports and uses power_grid_model (PowerGridModel, CalculationMethod) and power_grid_model_io to load the JSON data
The solution calls model.calculate_power_flow() with batch update data rather than interpreting the pre-computed file directly
A convergence status table is produced covering all batch scenarios with a solved/failed flag
Per-scenario KPIs (min/max u_pu, max branch loading, active losses) are computed from the freshly calculated output arrays
The maximum absolute deviation of u_pu between the newly calculated and pre-computed reference results is reported numerically

evals.title: Run Batch State Estimation and Benchmark Against Ground Truth
evals.prompt: Run state estimation on the network and check how well it matches the true power flow. Show me the worst estimates and a plot of errors over time.
evals.expected_output: A Python script that executes batch state estimation via PowerGridModel.calculate_state_estimation(), computes per-step RMSE against the ground-truth file, identifies the worst-estimated nodes, and saves a time-series plot.
expectations: The solution calls model.calculate_state_estimation() with CalculationMethod.iterative_linear rather than reading the pre-computed SE output file
A step-level convergence summary table is produced (solved / non-finite / diverged per scenario)
Per-step RMSE of u_pu is computed by comparing estimated node voltages against the ground-truth power flow output
The 5 nodes with the highest mean absolute u_pu error over all 192 steps are identified by node ID
A time-series plot of mean absolute voltage error per step is saved as a PNG file

evals.title: Short Circuit Calculation with IEC 60909
evals.prompt: Calculate short circuit faults on the network. Find the riskiest nodes and which branches would be affected.
evals.expected_output: A Python script that calls PowerGridModel.calculate_short_circuit() with IEC 60909 settings, a CSV of all node fault currents ranked by magnitude, branch overload analysis for top-5 fault nodes, and a markdown summary file.
expectations: The solution imports ShortCircuitVoltageScaling and CalculationMethod from power_grid_model and calls model.calculate_short_circuit() — this cannot be answered without the PGM library
Fault current magnitudes are extracted from the short circuit output node arrays (i_a, i_b, i_c or the three-phase equivalent)
All nodes are ranked by fault current and the result is saved to a CSV file
Branch overload analysis for the top-5 fault nodes is performed using branch output arrays from the same calculation
A markdown summary file identifying the highest-risk nodes is saved to the outputs directory

evals.title: PGM-DS Topology Analysis — Radial/Meshed Detection and Feeder Depth
evals.prompt: Analyze the network topology. Is it radial or meshed? How deep are the branches? Are there any unusual connection points?
evals.expected_output: A Python script that builds a PGM-DS Grid, applies its built-in graph algorithms to classify topology, and saves a topology report with connected-component count, radial/meshed classification, max feeder depth, and high-degree node list.
expectations: The solution constructs a power_grid_model_ds Grid object from the loaded input data
Connected-component count is derived using PGM-DS graph methods, not external libraries
A radial vs meshed determination is made using cycle detection available in PGM-DS graph tools
Maximum feeder depth from the source node is computed and reported as a concrete number
A markdown topology report is saved to the outputs directory

evals.title: Batch Update Data Validation with assert_valid_batch_data
evals.prompt: Check if the batch updates are valid. Any problems with the scenarios? Summary of what gets updated.
evals.expected_output: A Python script that calls validate_batch_data or assert_valid_batch_data from power_grid_model.validation, produces scenario-level validation findings, applies realism thresholds from validation-rules.yml, and saves both a JSON and a markdown report.
expectations: The solution imports and calls validate_batch_data or assert_valid_batch_data from power_grid_model.validation — this is a PGM-specific API that general LLMs cannot replicate
Scenario-level validation results are reported with specific PGM error codes or messages where failures exist
The realism check for sym_load p_specified and q_specified uses numeric thresholds from validation-rules.yml, not arbitrary guesses
A per-component-type update count table is produced from the update data arrays
Both a JSON and a markdown summary are saved to the outputs directory

evals.title: Newton-Raphson vs Iterative-Current Method Comparison
evals.prompt: Try two different calculation methods on the same network. How different are the results? Which one seems better?
evals.expected_output: A Python script that runs PowerGridModel.calculate_power_flow() with both CalculationMethod.newton_raphson and CalculationMethod.iterative_current, computes per-node and per-branch differences numerically, and saves a markdown comparison table with a method recommendation.
expectations: The solution calls model.calculate_power_flow() twice — once per calculation method — so that both result sets are derived by running PGM, not by reading a cached file
Per-node u_pu deviations between the two methods are computed numerically and the maximum deviation is reported
The 10 most loaded branches are identified under each method using branch output arrays
Source active and reactive power outputs are reported for both methods
A justified method recommendation (e.g. based on network size, convergence behavior, or deviation magnitude) is included in the output markdown

evals.title: N-1 Contingency Screening via Programmatically Constructed Batch Updates
evals.prompt: Simulate losing each branch one at a time. Which outages are the most critical? Rank them and show which ones cause problems.
evals.expected_output: A Python script that uses initialize_array to build the N-1 batch update data from scratch, runs batch power flow with continue_on_batch_error=True, and saves a contingency ranking CSV and a markdown summary of critical outages.
expectations: The solution imports and calls initialize_array from power_grid_model to construct the batch update arrays — this is the PGM-specific API that general LLMs will not know; using manually built numpy dtypes or wrong field names will cause a runtime error
Branch status fields are set using the exact PGM field name 'status' (not 'enabled', 'active', or 'in_service') with value 0 to take each branch out of service

model.calculate_power_flow() is called with update_data built from initialize_array and with continue_on_batch_error=True so diverged (islanded) scenarios are captured rather than raising an exception
Voltage violations are counted per scenario by checking node u_pu output arrays against the [0.95, 1.05] band
A contingency ranking CSV sorted by total violations (voltage violations + branch overloads) is saved to the outputs directory alongside a markdown top-5 summary

evals.title: SE Measurement Residual Analysis and Sensor Flagging
evals.prompt: Look at state estimation measurement residuals. Which sensors are off? Do the measurements look calibrated correctly?
evals.expected_output: A Python script that executes state estimation via PGM, extracts and normalizes residuals, produces per-sensor statistics with 3-sigma flags, saves histogram plots, and interprets residual distribution calibration quality.
expectations: The solution calls model.calculate_state_estimation() to produce fresh SE outputs rather than reading the pre-computed output file
Residuals are extracted from the sym_voltage_sensor and sym_power_sensor output arrays (u_residual, p_residual, q_residual fields)
Each residual is normalized by the corresponding sigma value from the input sensor data
A per-sensor statistics table (mean, std, max, 3-sigma flag) is produced covering all 192 steps
Residual histograms for each sensor type are saved as a PNG file and the normality of the distribution is commented on
